subject: Is it possible to introduce new parameters in the constraint section?

messages.author: 1e94001192669559
messages.subject: Is it possible to introduce new parameters in the constraint section?
parts:
Hi folks.
Apologies for a newbie post.
I'm trying to fit a nonlinear growth model (e.g., a gompertz curve with a random intercept component.)
I would like to introduce two new paramters (alpha and lambda) for the nonlinear optimization. 
I know that certain computer programs that rhyme with Nplus can accommodate this with a new statement
such as New(alpha, lambda)
but don't see a comparable way to do this in Lavaan.
Here is the lavaan code I'm trying to write now:
gompertzRI.model <-'
  int =~ 1*t0 + 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4 + 1*t5
  slope =~ lambda0*t0 + lambda1*t1 + lambda2*t2 + lambda3*t3 + lambda4*t4 + lambda5*t5
int ~~ int
slope ~~ 1*slope
t0 ~ 0*1
t1 ~ 0*1
t2 ~ 0*1
t3 ~ 0*1
t4 ~ 0*1
t5 ~ 0*1
int ~ 1
slope ~1
lambda0 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (1-lambda)))
lambda1 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (2-lambda)))
lambda2 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (3-lambda)))
lambda3 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (4-lambda)))
lambda4 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (5-lambda)))
lambda5 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (6-lambda)))
'
which is somewhat analogous to the following Mplus code which does work:

s by t0* 0.00000000 (L0)
t1* 0.00004928 (L1)
t2* 0.19409193 (L2)
t3* 0.76262042 (L3)
t4* 0.95619334 (L4)
t5* 0.99262276 (L5) ;
I by t0@1
t1@1
t2@1
t3@1
t4@1
t5@1 ;
[t0*] (int0);
[t1*] (int1);
[t2*] (int2);
[t3*] (int3);
[t4*] (int4);
[t5*] (int5);
t0* 0.052631579 ;
t1* 0.052631579 ;
t2* 0.054614299 ;
t3* 0.083241574 ;
t4* 0.100752932 ;
t5* 0.104489471 ;
[i* 10 ] (imean);
[s* 1 ] (smean);
i* 1 (ivar);
s* 1 (svar);
I with s*0 (cov);
model constraint:
new(alpha*.5,lambda*5);
svar=1;
cov=0;
int0=0;
int1=0;
int2=0;
int3=0;
int4=0;
int5=0;
L0= EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (1-lambda)));
L1= EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (2-lambda)));
L2= EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (3-lambda)));
L3= EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (4-lambda)));
L4= EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (5-lambda)));
L5= EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (6-lambda)));

TIA for your patience. Phil

Phil—

     You want the lavaan new parameter operator, :=

See:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html

for an example of this operator in use.

--Ed Rigdon

Hi folks.

Apologies for a newbie post.

I'm trying to fit a nonlinear growth model (e.g., a gompertz curve with a random intercept component.)

I would like to introduce two new paramters (alpha and lambda) for the nonlinear optimization. 

I know that certain computer programs that rhyme with Nplus can accommodate this with a new statement

such as New(alpha, lambda)

but don't see a comparable way to do this in Lavaan.

Here is the lavaan code I'm trying to write now:

gompertzRI.model <-'

  int =~ 1*t0 + 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4 + 1*t5

  slope =~ lambda0*t0 + lambda1*t1 + lambda2*t2 + lambda3*t3 + lambda4*t4 + lambda5*t5

int ~~ int

slope ~~ 1*slope

t0 ~ 0*1

t1 ~ 0*1

t2 ~ 0*1

t3 ~ 0*1

t4 ~ 0*1

t5 ~ 0*1

int ~ 1

slope ~1

lambda0 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (1-lambda)))

lambda1 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (2-lambda)))

lambda2 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (3-lambda)))

lambda3 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (4-lambda)))

lambda4 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (5-lambda)))

lambda5 == EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (6-lambda)))

'

which is somewhat analogous to the following Mplus code which does work:

 

s by t0*           0.00000000     (L0)    

t1*       0.00004928     (L1)    

t2*       0.19409193     (L2)    

t3*       0.76262042     (L3)    

t4*       0.95619334     (L4)    

t5*       0.99262276     (L5)     ;

I by t0@1                               

t1@1                          

t2@1                          

t3@1                          

t4@1                          

t5@1   ;                      

[t0*] (int0);                            

[t1*] (int1);                            

[t2*] (int2);                            

[t3*] (int3);                            

[t4*] (int4);                            

[t5*] (int5);                            

t0*       0.052631579   ;          

t1*       0.052631579   ;          

t2*       0.054614299   ;          

t3*       0.083241574   ;          

t4*       0.100752932   ;          

t5*       0.104489471   ;          

[i*       10        ] (imean);       

[s*       1          ] (smean);      

i*         1          (ivar); 

s*        1          (svar);

I with s*0 (cov);                                

model constraint:                              

new(alpha*.5,lambda*5);                              

svar=1;                                   

cov=0;                        

int0=0;                       

int1=0;                       

int2=0;                       

int3=0;                       

int4=0;                       

int5=0;                       

L0=     EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (1-lambda)));                    

L1=     EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (2-lambda)));                    

L2=     EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (3-lambda)));                    

L3=     EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (4-lambda)));                    

L4=     EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (5-lambda)));                    

L5=     EXP (-1 * EXP (-alpha * (6-lambda)));                    

 

TIA for your patience. Phil

On 04/04/2015 08:48 PM, Phil Wood wrote:
> I would like to introduce two new paramters (alpha and lambda) for the
> nonlinear optimization.

I am afraid lavaan (0.5-18) can not do this (for now). The ":=" operator
only defines new parameters as a function of existing *model* parameters.

But in your Mplus code, 'alpha' and 'lambda' only appear in the
constraints section, not in the model.

Still, I may give this a try. Could you send me an example dataset
(perhaps simulated), and the Mplus output for this model? I will see if
I can implement this in lavaan.

Yves.

Hi folks.

Apologies for a newbie post.

I'm trying to fit a nonlinear growth model (e.g., a gompertz curve with a random intercept component.)

I would like to introduce two new paramters (alpha and lambda) for the nonlinear optimization. 

I know that certain computer programs that rhyme with Nplus can accommodate this with a new statement

such as New(alpha, lambda)

but don't see a comparable way to do this in Lavaan.

Here is the lavaan code I'm trying to write now:

gompertzRI.model <-'

On 04/06/2015 07:10 PM, Phil Wood wrote:
> So if I need to both free and name a parameter, how do I do that? z.Bl.,
> slope =~ lambda0*NA*t0

You can mention the same rhs element several times with a different
'modifier':

slope =~ lambda0*t0 + NA*t0

Yves.

messages.author: 1e94001192669559
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to introduce new parameters in the constraint section?
parts:
Thanks so much, Yves & Ed!
I apologize for working my way through such a simple example.

By way of payment to the group, then, here is the code in lavaan which uses two phantom variables and a comparison of the obtained estimates to Mplus estimates as well as their bias.
Following this coding strategy then, here's what the simple example code would look like using a phantom variable strategy which appears to recover the parameter loaidings identically to Mplus.
The output which I receive is somewhat odd in that the degrees of freedom are incorrect, though, and in order for lavaan to correctly estimate what the nonlinearly constrained loadings are, I needed ot start it out with a very favorable initial estimate.

---------------------------------------

gompertzRI.model <-'
   int =~ 1*t0 + 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4 + 1*t5

slope =~ NA*t0 + lmb0*t0 + lmb1*t1 + lmb2*t2 + lmb3*t3 +
lmb4*t4 + lmb5*t5

int ~~ int
slope ~~ 1*slope

int ~~ 0*slope
phant1 =~ 0*t0
phant2 =~ 0*t0
phant1 ~ lambda*1 + start(3.274)*1
phant2 ~ alpha*1 + start(1.738)*1
phant1 ~~ 0*phant1
phant2 ~~ 0*phant2
phant1 ~~ 0*phant2
phant1 ~~ 0*int
phant1 ~~ 0*slope
phant2 ~~ 0*int
phant2 ~~ 0*slope

t0 ~ 0*1
t1 ~ 0*1
t2 ~ 0*1
t3 ~ 0*1
t4 ~ 0*1
t5 ~ 0*1
int ~ 1
slope ~1

lmb0 := exp(-1 * exp(-alpha * (1-lambda)))
lmb1 := exp(-1 * exp(-alpha * (2-lambda)))
lmb2 := exp(-1 * exp(-alpha * (3-lambda)))
lmb3 := exp(-1 * exp(-alpha * (4-lambda)))
lmb4 := exp(-1 * exp(-alpha * (5-lambda)))
lmb5 := exp(-1 * exp(-alpha * (6-lambda)))
'
fitgompRI <- sem(gompertzRI.model, data = sixtime)
summary(fitgompRI, standardized = TRUE)
unclass( coef(fitgompRI) )

Oddly, you'll notice that lavaan returns the free basis loadings in the report of parameter estimates, but correctly reports the nonlinearly constrained loadings.
I'm a bit puzzled by that as well as the reported chi square which lavaan reports as having 10 degrees of freedom when it should have 16, though the chi square value estimated is correct.
Similarly, I don't know if I can believe the estimates of lavaan of alpha and lambda, given that those are the final values from Mplus.
If anyone has insights into this, I'd love to learn more.
thanks!
